chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When the sun is totally eclipsed and obscured, and you did not know, then you came to know after that, so upon you is the making up (of the missed prayer); and if it did not become totally obscured, so there is no making up upon you.

And in another report, when one knows of the eclipse and forgets to pray, so upon him is the making up; and if he did not know of it, so there is no making up upon him. This is when the whole of it is not totally obscured.

key_terms.احْتَرَقَتْ: It was consumed/obscured (idiomatically used for total eclipse in this context)

ai.seo_question: When is the eclipse prayer obligatory to make up if missed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the conditions for Qada (making up) the Salat al-Kusuf, distinguishing between total and partial eclipses while accounting for human forgetfulness or ignorance. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that negligence is excused if the cause (the eclipse) was not perceived, yet obligation remains if the event was total and missed due to oversight. This ruling underscores the balance between divine command and practical human limitation in ritual observance.
